title: Re-Reading Is Not Free: Token Traces and Cache-Aware Energy Estimation for LLM Agents in Software Engineering
abstract: arXiv:2611.20873v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) evolve from conversational assistants into autonomous agents embedded in software development workflows, estimating their environmental footprint requires moving beyond conventional token-based accounting. Existing energy estimators focus on isolated request-response interactions, overlooking the repeated processing of accumulated context, cache reuse, and work delegated to subagents. We analyze nearly one billion tokens collected across 42 sessions and 752 task episodes over ten weeks of real-world AI-assisted software development. Cached-context reads make up 94.8% of all API-reported tokens, while uncached input accounts for only 0.017%; for every generated token, approximately 260 cached tokens are read. Context grows 5.3-fold over a session compared with 1.4-fold within individual tasks. To quantify the energy implications, we extend an existing analytical inference-energy model to account for cache

translated_title: 重读并非免费：软件工程中LLM智能体的Token轨迹与缓存感知能耗估计
translated_abstract: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）从对话助手演变为嵌入软件开发工作流中的自主智能体，估算其环境足迹需要超越传统的基于token的计量方式。现有的能耗估计器聚焦于孤立的请求-响应交互，忽视了对累积上下文的重复处理、缓存复用以及委托给子智能体的工作。我们分析了在十周真实AI辅助软件开发过程中收集的近10亿个token，这些数据涵盖42个会话和752个任务片段。缓存上下文读取占API报告token总数的94.8%，而非缓存输入仅占0.017%；每生成一个token，大约需要读取260个缓存token。与单个任务内1.4倍的上下文增长相比，整个会话期间上下文增长了5.3倍。为了量化其能耗影响，我们扩展了现有的分析式推理能耗模型，以纳入缓存相关的因素。
tldr: 该论文基于十周真实AI辅助软件开发中近10亿token的分析，发现缓存上下文读取占LLM智能体token总量的94.8%（每生成一个token需读取约260个缓存token），并据此提出了纳入缓存复用与子智能体工作的缓存感知能耗估计模型。
en_tdlr: Analyzing nearly one billion tokens from ten weeks of real-world AI-assisted software development, this paper reveals that cached-context reads account for 94.8% of LLM agent tokens (about 260 cached tokens read per generated token) and proposes a cache-aware energy estimation model that incorporates cache reuse and subagent delegation.
